Troops rescue three kidnapped victims along Okene bypass in Kogi

By: Zagazola Makama

Troops of Sector 1, Operation Whirl Stroke (OPWS), have rescued three kidnapped victims following a swift response to a kidnapping incident along the Okene bypass in Okene Local Government Area of Kogi State.

Security sources told Zagazola Makama that the incident occurred at about 12:17 a.m. on Tuesday, Oct. 6, when troops deployed at Forward Operating Base (FOB) Adogo responded to a report of kidnapping along the route.

The troops arrived at the scene and found an abandoned vehicle whose occupants were suspected to have been kidnapped.

They subsequently trailed the route taken by the kidnappers. The criminals, upon sighting the advancing troops, reportedly abandoned three victims and fled into the surrounding area.

One of the rescued victims sustained a gunshot wound and was evacuated to a hospital for medical attention.

The other two victims were assisted by the troops to continue their journey after being rescued.

Security personnel are continuing efforts to track the fleeing kidnappers and prevent further criminal activities along the Okene bypass.

Ekiti State Police Command  detain officers following allegations of extortion, during a stop-and-search operation involving a biker affiliated with the Federal University Oye-Ekiti.

The development followed the circulation of a video on social media showing an encounter between the biker and a police patrol team, which triggered public outrage and calls for an investigation into the conduct of the officers.

The command, in a statement issued on Wednesday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Abutu Sunday, said it commenced investigation after receiving a formal complaint from representatives of the Biker Association, Federal University Oye-Ekiti Chapter.

According to the statement, the complaint was lodged at the Ilupeju Ekiti Police Division on October 6, 2026, concerning an alleged incident involving one of the association’s members.

The biker was reportedly travelling alone from Itapa to Ikole-Ekiti when he was intercepted by a police patrol team.

The complainants alleged that the officers demanded money from the biker under circumstances they considered improper, while also accusing the personnel of intimidation, disobedience to lawful orders and other acts of misconduct.

The command said it immediately commenced preliminary inquiries and subsequently identified and detained the officers involved for questioning.

It added that the matter had been transferred to the State Police Headquarters in Ado-Ekiti for a discreet, comprehensive and impartial investigation.

“The circumstances surrounding the alleged extortion, intimidation and other acts of unprofessional conduct are being thoroughly investigated,” the command stated.

The Commissioner of Police, Falade Adegoroye Micheal, was said to have directed that the officers be subjected to appropriate disciplinary procedures in accordance with the regulations and disciplinary provisions of the Nigeria Police Force, depending on the outcome of the investigation.

The command stressed that no police officer was authorised to demand or collect money from members of the public under any guise while performing legitimate police duties.

It condemned extortion, intimidation, abuse of authority and other forms of misconduct capable of eroding public confidence in the police.

The police authorities said officers found culpable of abuse of office, misconduct or violation of established regulations would face appropriate sanctions.

The command also appealed to members of the public to report cases of alleged police misconduct through established channels, assuring residents that credible complaints would be investigated.

The police said the latest investigation was part of the command’s commitment to professionalism, discipline, accountability and respect for citizens’ fundamental rights.

SEVEN PASSENGERS REPORTEDLY SHOT NEAR BUKURU ROUNDABOUT IN PLATEAU

Seven passengers travelling from the Kara Bukuru Livestock Market were reportedly shot by unidentified gunmen near the Total Roundabout in Bukuru, Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The incident reportedly occurred around 6:30 p.m. on Sunday, October 4, 2026, as the passengers travelled in an open-body Boxer vehicle from the market to Rafin Bauna village in Bassa Local Government Area.

Sources said the vehicle was carrying 20 passengers when the gunmen opened fire.

A survivor, identified as Murtala Isa Ibrahim, and the driver reportedly confirmed that seven passengers were affected in the attack.

The victims were subsequently taken to Rukuba Barracks Hospital for medical attention. Their conditions were, however, not immediately known.

No death had been confirmed as of the time of filing this report, while the circumstances surrounding the shooting remained unclear.

The latest incident comes amid growing concerns over attacks reportedly targeting herders and other travellers returning from the Kara Bukuru Livestock Market.

Meanwhile, a pastoralist association in Plateau State has condemned a separate reported attack on Fulani herders around the Federal Low-Cost area of Bukuru and called on security agencies to investigate the incident.

The association recalled that five Fulani herders were reportedly killed around Kassa in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area on September 20 while returning from the same market.

It also cited an earlier attack near the Conoil Filling Station in December 2025 involving herders returning from the livestock market.

The recurring incidents have raised concerns about the safety of pastoralists, traders and other residents who depend on the market for their livelihoods.

The association urged the Plateau State Government, the Nigeria Police Force, Operation Safe Haven, the Department of State Services and other security agencies to strengthen security along the market route and prevent further attacks.

It also appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid retaliatory violence, stressing the need for justice and equal protection for all, regardless of ethnicity or occupation.

As of the time of filing this report, no official statement had been issued by security authorities confirming the latest shooting.

The details of the incident therefore remain preliminary and subject to independent verification.
